items.title: Price pressures persisted in October
items.snippet: Data: Bureau of Labor Statistics ; Chart: Courtenay Brown/Axios Inflation remained hot in October, according to data from the Labor Department released on Tuesday. Why it matters: The Consumer Price Index shows that even as gasoline prices steadied, inflation pressures elsewhere remained stubborn. By the numbers: CPI rose 0.4% last month, slowing from the 0.6% increase in September. Gasoline prices gained 1% in October, a sharp slowdown from the 9.1% surge in September, the Labor Department said. Core CPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, advanced 0.3% for the third straight month, with higher prices for recreation, medical care, car insurance and airline fares contributing to the increase. Of note: The Labor Department did not publish year-over-year inflation rates for October. Last year's government shutdown left a gap in the data that prevents direct comparisons with October 2025. But if one assumes the October 2025 readings were halfway between September and November, year-over-year inflation comes to 4% — or 2.8% excluding food and energy. items.title: Amazon and Google Win Big From Anthropic IPO
items.snippet: If you’re looking for a cheaper way of getting exposure to Anthropic than buying the stock directly, consider Amazon or Google. Anthropic’s updated IPO filing on Tuesday shows just how many shares each of those two tech giants will own in Anthropic, along with how much money they’re making on their early investments in the AI firm. Neither tech giant will own voting shares in Anthropic, so antitrust cops won’t have to worry about their influence over its management. But their stakes are significant. In theory, Amazon could own around 20% of Anthropic’s outstanding shares. But because of a self-imposed ownership cap, Amazon won’t hold more than 12% of Anthropic. The rest of its holdings are convertible notes that can convert to equity over time. Regardless, Amazon’s economic return is pretty damn good. Forgetting about the ownership cap for a minute, Amazon’s entire 20%-or-so stake would be worth about $258 billion at the midpoint of Anthropic’s proposed IPO pricing range. That’s from an investment totaling around $18.6 billion. (Anthropic’s final IPO price may well end up higher than the preliminary range, a Financial Times report tonight suggests).

items.title: The Anthropic-OpenAI Valuation Gap
items.snippet: If you want proof of the widening gap in sentiment between public and private investors, take a look at the valuations of Anthropic and OpenAI. On Tuesday, Anthropic disclosed it was targeting a valuation of between $1.26 trillion and $1.4 trillion in its upcoming initial public offering. The prospectus update comes on the heels of OpenAI’s most recent fundraising, which valued the company at $1.25 trillion . That means Anthropic expects public investors to value it at only 12% more than OpenAI, assuming it achieves the valuation at the high end of its range. That is in spite of the fact that Anthropic generated 70% revenue than OpenAI in the third quarter and has been growing far faster for much of this year. Still, Anthropic’s advisers may be guiding the valuation downward now to make sure there’s plenty of demand for the stock on the first day of trading. There’s a good chance Anthropic can increase the IPO price or sell even more shares if investors’ demand is strong, as some Anthropic investors are expecting.
